body:
Last night on Predictable, we spent a lot of time talking about something that’s really important if you’re going to survive in prediction markets long term:
Not every losing position is actually a bad trade. That sounds insane at first. Especially if you’re new to this stuff. You put money into a position. The position loses. End of story, right?
Not exactly.
Sometimes the value is in understanding the signal before everybody else does.
The Louisiana Lesson
That’s basically what happened in Louisiana.
We talked last week about Bill Cassidy being politically dead long before the final results officially came in. The market already understood what was happening: when Donald Trump decides he wants someone removed in a Republican primary, that person suddenly has a very serious problem.
The interesting part wasn’t just Cassidy losing.
It was how the race moved.
The polling averages had Julia Letlow sitting in the low 30s. She wound up surging more than ten points higher than where the averages suggested. She didn’t quite hit the 50% threshold we were targeting on one of the long-shot positions, but the underlying thesis was still right:
Trump-aligned voters consolidated late. Fast.
That matters going forward.
Because now the exact same dynamic may be unfolding again in Kentucky with Thomas Massie.
The Massie Question
And honestly, this one is more complicated.
I like Thomas Massie. I said that pretty directly on the show last night. He’s one of the few politicians who actually seems to operate from a coherent worldview instead of whatever focus group tested well that morning. Even when I disagree with him, I respect that consistency.
But prediction markets don’t care who you personally like.
They care about incentives. Power. Coalitions. Momentum.
And right now, the market is trying to answer one big question:
What happens when Trump really wants somebody gone?
That’s where things get interesting.
Massie spent most of this race comfortably ahead. Then suddenly, over the last few weeks, the market started flipping hard toward Ed Gallen after Trump escalated publicly against Massie. That shift matters more than the media narrative. Because one thing we’re learning over and over in these Republican primaries is this: 
Trump’s endorsement power is probably still being underpriced.
Not universally. Not in every race. But enough to matter. And that’s where prediction markets become useful. The goal isn’t to perfectly predict every election. The goal is to identify when the market is still catching up to reality.
The Media vs Prediction Markets
We also spent part of the show breaking down the new 60 Minutes “prediction market insider trading” panic segment, which mostly revealed something important:
These companies (Polymarket, Kalshi, etc) actually have enormous incentives to police bad actors themselves.
The media keeps trying to frame prediction markets as some sort of unregulated casino filled with secret insiders. But the irony is that prediction markets are often more transparent than the institutions criticizing them. Every trade on PolyMarket is visible publicly on-chain. The suspicious activity gets noticed incredibly quickly.
That doesn’t mean bad actors don’t exist.
It means the ecosystem actually has incentives to find them.
Which is very different from most of modern media.
Also…
We briefly touched on:
why “good losses” matter in long-term trading
why primary polling is much weaker than general election polling
why Trump’s influence behaves differently in primaries
why Massie may actually fit the definition of “RINO” better than people realize (though probably not in the way Trump means it)
and somehow… Gina Carano getting submitted by Ronda Rousey in 17 seconds.
As one does.
Anyway, if you missed last night’s episode, definitely check out the full episode (linked at the top of this article). We’re heading into another big primary night and there are several markets setting up right now that are worth paying attention to.
If you’re enjoying learning about prediction markets and seeing how we break down the signals behind the headlines, consider sharing Predictable with a friend and helping us build this community from the ground up.
You’re part of the early group shaping what this becomes, and we’re excited to have you on board with us!
